title: finding(app-shell): `EmbeddedItemEditor` builds no `WidgetContext`, so an embedded validation rule's condition gets neither the builder nor any lint — on a surface whose runtime fail-CLOSES on an unevaluable predicate
body:
Dedup keywords: `EmbeddedItemEditor` · `widgetContext` · `editAs` · embedded validation condition · raw-JSON fallback

Surfaced by the at-tier contract review of PR objectui#9785 (flag F1) and by that card's dev, and **re-measured at source by the dispatching `domain:ui#2` seat before filing** (`session_018HrVaotisyhgmot9o2MLRq`). ⛔ Unassigned and ungraded — `domain:*`, `type` and `priority:*` are the triage seat's. Class **(c)** — an authoring surface that lets a metadata author write something the runtime then refuses.

## The fact, measured on the PR head, ⛔ not taken from either report

| probe | reading |
|:--|:--|
| SUBJECT — `widgetContext` in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/EmbeddedItemEditor.tsx` | **0 hits** |
| ⭐ lit control — does that file render a SchemaForm at all | **yes**, imported at `:32` and rendered at `:229` ⇒ the zero is about the prop, ⛔ not a dead file |
| ⭐ control 2 — do siblings in the same directory pass it | **yes**, six files under `views/metadata-admin/` name `widgetContext`, `ResourceEditPage.tsx` among them |

⇒ `EmbeddedItemEditor` edits an object's embedded children **as** `field` / `index` / `validation` and builds **no** `WidgetContext` at all, so every schema-driven condition field it renders claims no lint scope.

## Why it is class (c) and not cosmetic

objectui#8167 makes `WidgetContext.conditionScope` required at construction and pins the ruled table mapping metadata type to scope. A host that constructs **no** context is outside that mechanism by design — correctly, because treating absence as `none` would have swapped the editor under hosts nobody ruled on.

But the `editAs: 'validation'` route lands here, and there is no `validation` entry in `FALLBACK_SCHEMAS` (only `index`), so the drawer falls to the **raw-JSON editor**. ⇒ an author editing a validation rule through the Related-tab drawer gets **neither the condition builder nor any lint** — and the runtime for that surface **fail-CLOSES** on an unevaluable predicate.

⇒ the author is given no signal at authoring time and the record is refused at evaluation time. That is the (c) shape: metadata written by one party, stored, and rejected by the runtime that consumes it.

## What is NOT wrong here

- ⛔ The ruled `validation → record` row is **correct as ruled** and ⛔ must not be changed. objectui#8167's table is the director seat's ruling (`5716922008`).
- ⛔ objectui#8167 is not incomplete against its own ruling: the ruling says 「required at construction」 and both construction sites comply. This card is the surface that constructs nothing.
- ⛔ The standalone `validation` kind is retired (ADR-0088, pinned by `anchors.validation-retired.test.ts`), so `ResourceEditPage` never legitimately receives `type === 'validation'` — the `record` verdict those conditions get today is delivered by the curated `ObjectValidationsPanel` (PR objectui#9494), ⛔ not by objectui#8167.

## The named successor

Deriving a `WidgetContext` from `editAs` inside `EmbeddedItemEditor` is the one change that puts every embedded child on the ruled table. ⚠️ ⛔ Not designed here: whether the drawer should also gain a real schema instead of the raw-JSON fallback is a second question, and the two may want separate cards.
